claims.text: A reactive additive can form ceramic reinforcement particles in situ during spark plasma sintering at approximately 1700 °C.
Applying this intervention to ZrB2 will improve structural integrity relative to both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Applying this intervention to ZrB2 will improve oxidation durability relative to both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Applying this intervention to ZrB2 will improve liquid-metal corrosion resistance relative to both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
A minor ZrO2-forming or carbide-forming reagent will react during ZrB2 spark plasma sintering to produce uniformly dispersed fine particles.
Spark plasma sintering near 1700 °C under pressure of tens of MPa can produce an in-situ particle-reinforced composite.
The proposed processing conditions will adequately densify the ZrB2-based material.
The intervention will create uniformly distributed, fine ceramic particles within the ZrB2 matrix.
The secondary particles will pin grain boundaries and refine the ZrB2 grain structure.
The secondary particles will strengthen the ZrB2 composite.
The secondary particles will act as barriers to oxidation.
The secondary particles will impede penetration by liquid plating metals.
The composite processed near 1700 °C will have mechanical strength and structural integrity on par with or exceeding single-phase ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C.
The composite will have better oxidation resistance than lower-temperature single-phase ZrB2 specimens.
The composite will have better liquid-metal corrosion resistance than lower-temperature single-phase ZrB2 specimens.
Previously reported lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens lack a reinforcing secondary phase.
The absence of a reinforcing secondary phase causes reduced oxidation durability and corrosion resistance in prior lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens.
The proposed composite can remain compatible with prolonged service in liquid plating-metal environments.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows mechanical performance merely on par with high-temperature single-phase ZrB2, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant strength improvement over that control. An on-par result could therefore satisfy the prediction while triggering falsification.

The main hypothesis claims improvements in structural integrity, oxidation durability, and corrosion resistance relative to both comparison groups, while the predicted-outcome field only requires strength parity or superiority against high-temperature ZrB2 and only states oxidation and corrosion superiority against lower-temperature specimens.
